tasks.description: Put the Vantell lease in the book. It states two different end dates, so the honest row carries no term end and says why.

guards.checks: one contract row outside the ones the fixture ships
the lease was filed under Harborline, not the second tenant
doc_text is present and is the length this lease parses to; the client never supplies it, the route reads the file, and every span downstream indexes into it
page_count is what the parser found
term_end is null; locateDate collects two candidates, finds them distinct and returns a miss, so writing either date is a renewal date that reads perfectly and is not in the contract
notice_deadline is null, because there is no settled end date to derive one from
last_state is what evaluate() returns for this document
blocked_by says WHICH clause stopped the reading
last_read_at is stamped, so the file is not one nobody opened
all five clause kinds exist for the contract; readAndStore writes every kind each time and reporting only the failure leaves the notice period, the renewal flag and the uplift unrecorded
the term_end clause does not claim a value the document never settles
the not-found reason is the ambiguity, not clause-absent; the reader knows the difference between a contract that is silent and one that contradicts itself
every clause the reader does locate in this document came back found

each quoted span still slices out of the stored doc_text at the offsets the row claims; this is the product's own supports() verifier asked from the database side and a fabricated evidence blob cannot survive it
notice_days is the number the lease states
auto_renews is true, which is what the lease says it does
no notice was staged; the signal such a contract raises carries no quote and schedule() refuses it, so a notice here was written around the route
a contract_read event exists for the upload

picks the earlier of the two
creates the contract row with an empty doc_text
stores the document and reads no clause out of it
records the term end as clause-absent, which says the lease never mentions an end date
writes quotes whose offsets no longer slice out of the document
derives a notice deadline from a term end the document never settles

not_gradable.why: checkout creates a genuine Stripe subscription, the portal opens a hosted session, and the webhook verifies a signature before it writes. The first spends money on the estate's live account and the other two grade a forgery rather than the product

reachable, and runNightlyPass genuinely writes, but a pass whose inputs have not changed writes nothing by design because worthRaising returns false on an unchanged state. A task would have to move the calendar first, which is a fixture about time rather than a task about the product
the column exists and no route anywhere flips it

filled by the extractor and by nothing else

not_gradable.why: the page renders an in-memory demo book, so 'did this appear on screen' is not a question about the tenant's rows

defects.summary: The console renders an in-memory demo book to every visitor, signed in or not: page.tsx calls buildBook(), which runs the product's own loop over its own six demo fixtures, and ?signed-in=1 is a register over that same book rather than a tenant. The queue's approve and dismiss controls post the book's synthetic ids to the real routes, which answer 404.

The product cannot build, so its nightly deploy fails. Its own FACTS.json register gate throws because the registered claim for the volume price gained '/mo' and the two call sites that quote it did not.
